# A function that is one field's read or write is ported onto that field's accessor

Status: `open` (the rule `wave-194/batch-3/run-1` followed; the spec change is not made).

## Signal

A case the how-to skills leave unspecified, which a port had to settle by hand (`evolution`
§2). `porting-symbols`' Functions section gives a ported function "the safe API
`binding-symbols`' Functions section gives a function", homed in the file its item names,
and the conventions' Anchors section allows one Rust item to stand in for several C items
only for a symbol alias and for the accessors of one field. Neither says what a port does
with a function whose whole body reads or writes one member of a struct whose layout is
already bound, with an accessor for that member, in another module's file: a new method
in the function's own home duplicates the accessor, and annotating the accessor puts the
function's anchor outside its home.

## Evidence

`wave-194/batch-3/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/api.c`, symbol route). Nine of api.c's functions,
`llhttp_get_type`, `llhttp_get_http_major`, `llhttp_get_http_minor`, `llhttp_get_method`,
`llhttp_get_status_code`, `llhttp_get_upgrade`, `llhttp_get_errno`,
`llhttp_get_error_reason` and `llhttp_get_error_pos`, are `return parser-><field>;`, and
`llhttp_set_error_reason` is `parser->reason = reason;`. `deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`
(`llhttp.c`'s file, wave-194/batch-0) already has `ParserRef::parser_type`, `http_major`,
… `reason`, `error_offset` and `ParserMut::set_reason` over those members. The three
X-macro generators `HTTP_ERRNO_GEN`, `HTTP_METHOD_GEN` and `HTTP_STATUS_GEN`, each `case
PREFIX##NAME: return <text>;`, are batch 1's `Errno::constant_name`, `Method::map_string`
and `Status::map_string`. The batch's task message asked for these to be ported "as the
parser's native API, without duplicating what `llhttp.rs` gives": the batch added each
function's `Replaces` anchor and alias to the existing accessor beside the member's
`Wraps` one, so that 13 of its 28 items stand in through items in `llhttp.rs`, not in
their home `api.rs`, and wrote native code only for the items with logic of their own
(`execute`, `pause`, the resumptions, the lenient setters, `debug_trace`).

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols` § Functions (the translator's to evolve), and the
conventions' Anchors § Several stand-ins, which should name the case.

## Change

Not made: no review run was available to this batch. In `porting-symbols` § Functions,
after the first paragraph:

> A function whose body only reads or writes one member, or returns a value an existing
> item of the safe API already gives, is ported as that item: the accessor or method
> carries the function's `Replaces` anchor and alias beside its own, wherever it is
> homed, and the port writes no second API. Its export, where remaining C calls it, is
> written in its own module's gateway, over that item.

And in the conventions' § 3.2, beside the symbol alias: "and the existing accessor or
method a ported function is, as `porting-symbols`' Functions section describes".

## Validation

None run: the rule is the one this batch followed; a rerun under it would produce the
same port.

## Review

None yet.

# The standard library's own macro expansions count as unsafe code outside the regions

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule agents work around, at a cost to the code (`evolution` §2). The conventions' Unsafe
regions section counts "every invocation of another crate's macro that expands to" an
`unsafe` block as unsafe code, so native code may not invoke one, and ffimap's
`code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions` reports such an expansion. That includes the
standard library's `format_args!` (behind `write!`, `writeln!` and `format!`) and
`thread_local!`, whose unsafety is std's own, sound for every input, and which no
convention asks a crate to justify.

## Evidence

Three workarounds in one module:

- `wave-194/batch-0/run-1`: the four `Unnamed*` errors' `Display` used `write!`; the first
  scan found four unsafe blocks outside the regions, and the impls were rewritten to write
  their parts one by one (dashboard Notes, batch 0).
- `wave-194/batch-1/run-1`: a `thread_local!` in native code was moved into `ffi_import`
  for the same count, though it touches no C.
- `wave-194/batch-3/run-1`: `ParserRef::debug_trace`'s line, built with `writeln!` from
  `{:p}`, `{}` and `{:02x}` arguments, gave two blocks outside the regions
  (`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`, the boundary scan's `--sites
  code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions`); it was rewritten without `format_args!`, a
  hand-written hexadecimal writer (`push_hex`) in place of `{:x}`.

## Destination

The spec, the conventions' Unsafe regions section (not the translator's: proposed), and
ffimap, whose count follows it: an option naming the crates whose macro expansions are
trusted (`--trusted-macro-crates core,alloc,std`), their blocks reported under a share of
their own rather than `outside_regions`.

## Change

Not made. In the conventions' § 2.1, after "such as one that mints a type over a C layout":
"The standard library's own macros, `format_args!` and those built on it, and
`thread_local!`, are not unsafe code of the crate: their expansions are std's, sound for
every input."

## Validation

None run. The rerun that would validate it: scan `wave-194/batch-3`'s tree before its
`push_hex` rewrite with the option, and see the two sites leave `outside_regions`.

## Review

None yet.

content.content:
# The packaging gate's procedure, for a crate whose dependencies are unpublished

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A procedure worked out by hand that a skill should state: `testing-gates`' Regressions
section says that a batch that changes the raw bindings packages the safe crate, "built
alone in bundled mode from the C it packages, with no build variant selected", and that
"each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source", but not how. The
direct form fails, and the steps that pass were found by trial.

## Evidence

`wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, which allowlists three functions), on base
`2216b0cd0`, the first packaging gate since the tree's change of 2026-11-13:

1. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo package --offline --allow-dirty` stops before verifying:
   `no matching package named glibc-bindings found` (crates.io index). The packaged
   manifest drops the Git source of `glibc-bindings` and the path of `ffibox`, keeping
   their versions, and the workspace's `[patch]` tables, keyed by those sources, do not
   apply to it.
2. `cargo package --offline --allow-dirty --no-verify --exclude-lockfile` packages (697
   files). Extracted under `crustify/tmp/`, the package's manifest needs an empty
   `[workspace]`, since the worktree's own encloses it, and
   `[patch.crates-io] glibc-bindings = { path = "/target/glibc-crustify" }` and
   `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }`.
3. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo build --offline` there then fails in CMake: PCRE2, then
   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.

## Change

Not made: the gate is not a translator's to change. The section would name the script,
and say that the patches and search paths stand in for what a dependent's host supplies.

## Validation

The run above, step by step: step 1 fails as quoted, steps 2 and 3 pass. A script is
validated by passing on that tree and failing, naming the library, without the search
paths.

input.command:
cat > crustify/tmp/notes.md <<'EOF'
### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` wave 194 batch 3: the parser's API

api.c's first `port` batch, the `symbol` route of its wave 194: 28 items, homed in
`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. Thirteen are a field's read or write, or a map's text, that
batches 0 and 1 already give in `llhttp.rs`, so they are ported as those items, which carry
each function's `Replaces` anchor and alias beside their own, and no second API is written:
`fn::llhttp_get_type`, `fn::llhttp_get_method` and `fn::llhttp_get_errno` are
`ParserRef::parser_type`, `method` and `error`, read as llhttp's enums; `llhttp_get_http_major`,
`llhttp_get_http_minor`, `llhttp_get_status_code` and `llhttp_get_upgrade` are `http_major`,
`http_minor`, `status_code` and `upgrade`; `llhttp_get_error_reason` and
`llhttp_set_error_reason` are `reason` and `set_reason`; `llhttp_get_error_pos` is
`error_offset`, which locates the position in a slice rather than return a pointer into a past
input. The generators `mac::HTTP_ERRNO_GEN`, `mac::HTTP_METHOD_GEN` and `mac::HTTP_STATUS_GEN`
(`case PREFIX##NAME: return <text>;` inside the name functions) are `Errno::constant_name`,
`Method::map_string` and `Status::map_string`. Those anchors sit in `llhttp.rs`, outside the
items' home (`crustify/evolution/port-onto-an-existing-accessor`). The rest is native code in
`api.rs`: `ParserMut::execute(&[u8]) -> Result<Parsed, ParseError>` (`llhttp_execute`, the name
batch 1 left free, over `parse`); `pause`, `resume` and `resume_after_upgrade`, each moving the
parser only from the state C expects (no error, `HPE_PAUSED`, `HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE`), the
reason kept as C keeps it; the ten `set_lenient_*(bool)` setters, each over its bit of
`llhttp_lenient_flags`, whose constants the raw bindings gain; and `ParserRef::debug_trace`.

`fn::llhttp__debug` is compiled on this build, unconditionally, into `api.c.o` (`nm` of the
`plain` archive defines it), but nothing calls it: `llhttp.c` was generated without llparse's
debug mode and holds no call (wavefront: no callers), and no header declares it. So it is
ported, native and unexported, as `debug_trace(&self, rest: &[u8], msg: &str) ->
io::Result<()>`. Its `fprintf(stderr, …)` keeps the `crustify-campaign` route
`dependencies.json` recommends for `fprintf` and `stderr`: the line goes through
`glibc-bindings`' `stderr()` and `FileRef::print`, one locked `fprintf` on C's own stream, in
order with the remaining C's writes there, which `std::io::stderr`, writing the descriptor,
would not keep. The borrow's contract holds for the call: no C of libgit2, its dependencies or
its tests assigns, closes, reopens or unlocks `stderr`. One C defect is not carried over: C
prints the next byte, a signed `char`, through `%02x`, so a byte of 0x80 or more prints
sign-extended (`ffffff80`), a value `%x` does not define; Rust prints two digits, documented
and kept by a `unit_priv` test. `abort` and `memset` are not used by this batch's items: in
api.c they are the name functions' and `llhttp_finish`'s `default: abort()` and
`llhttp_settings_init`'s `memset`, batch 4's, where the `std` route holds
(`std::process::abort`, a zeroed value). The line is built without `format_args!`, whose
expansion the first scan counted as two unsafe blocks outside the regions
(`crustify/evolution/std-macro-expansions-outside-regions`).

Six of the functions have C callers outside api.c, and are exported in the module's gateway,
`ffi_export`, under the new export feature `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, off:
`llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`
(`transports/httpparser.c`), and `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume` and `llhttp_get_error_reason`
(`transports/httpparser.h`'s macros, expanded in `httpclient.c`). Each is checked at compile
time against its raw binding (`[sys::<name>, <name>]`). `llhttp_execute`'s body runs in
`barrier`, a panic (`parse`'s refusals) reported as `HPE_INTERNAL`; the three that cannot fail
abort on one. `llhttp_get_error_pos` hands back the stored address unread. The others,
`llhttp_set_error_reason` (called only by api.c's own span dispatchers), the getters and the
lenient setters, have no C caller outside the module and are not exported. The gateway cannot
be linked in place of `api.c.o` before batch 4: the object also defines `llhttp_init` and the
23 dispatchers, which are still C. The raw bindings gain `llhttp_lenient_flags`, `llhttp_pause`,
`llhttp_resume`, `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the ten lenient
setters, for the signature checks and the equivalence tests. The 25 functions' pointer
findings are submitted to the ownership store.

Tests: 4 `unit_priv` (the trace line against `llhttp__debug`'s format, the high byte, the
flag conversion and its refusal), 14 `unit_pub` (`execute` against `parse` in every run size
and on a kept error; `pause`, `resume` and `resume_after_upgrade` from each state; a paused
parser reading nothing; a pause by a callback resumed at its error offset; an upgrade; a
callback that pauses and returns `0`, which pauses the next run; every lenient setter against
its bit, alone and together; a relaxed version check; `debug_trace`'s write and its refusal of
a NUL), 2 `ub_safe` (callbacks pausing, resuming, relaxing and tracing their parser mid-parse;
`execute` refused from a callback of its own parse, as `parse` is), 4 `equiv` (the three calls
from four states in every pair against C's, the whole parser after each; `execute` against
`llhttp_execute` over runs between pauses; the lenient setters against C's, `int` values C
reads as true included; `set_reason` against `llhttp_set_error_reason`), and 3 doctests. No
`ub_unsafe` suite: the batch adds no public `unsafe fn`. llhttp has no C tests in the tree,
so none is carried over.

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the base `300c14dfc` and on this tree, read with
`report.py` from each scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and
`unit_pub`; the pp cells are against the base's own figures, C / Rust lines `29.23`% /
`78.42`% (`ub_safe`), `20.11`% / `14.98`% (`ub_unsafe`), `44.41`% / `74.86`% (`equiv`),
`33.69`% / `87.84`% (unit) and `47.04`% / `98.67`% (total), since the base took the
working branch with `utf8.c`'s switch, which measured none. Worklist: `api.rs` 123 of 123
lines, 20 of 20 functions, 96 of 96 regions; the gateway is compiled out. `api.c` moves from
184 to 264 of its 283 lines and 43 to 54 of 55 functions: every function of the worklist runs
under `equiv` but `llhttp__debug`, which has no raw binding and no caller, and whose format
the `unit_priv` test checks instead. Of the parser's states the tests reach running, paused,
upgrade-paused and failed, and every transition the three calls make between them, inside and
outside a parse. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total` (`+259`) and
`code.tests.loc.total` (`+535`), its C LoC to the measured `89009`; `ported symbols` counts the
28. `+LoC` leaves out the regenerated `bindings.rs` (`+86`). The `loc` cell is wavefront's
`query dag --loc`.

The safety audit scans (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as wave 225's) name the export feature on
this tree and none on the base, which declares none: `raw→std` `+1` is the gateway's
`slice::from_raw_parts`, `raw deref` `+1` its read of `error_pos`, and of the nine new unsafe
blocks one is `ffi_import`'s `stderr()` borrow and eight `ffi_export`'s, seven of them the
exports' and left out of the cell. The boundary scan's sites hold none in the changeset: those
in the llhttp files are batch 0's `data` and `settings` accessors. `ffimap api` against the
base (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's with private items): the 28 items are `new`; the 15 keys
of the parser, its members and maps whose items gained anchors are `kept`; unattributed, only
`sys::libgit2` is extended, by 26 bindings.

Gates, on the base `300c14dfc`, the wave branch's tip: formatted (nightly rustfmt; `build.rs`'s
diff is the base's), and `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied with
the export feature off and on. The whole workspace passes on `plain` (`lib` 852 and 1
ignored, `equiv` 549, `ub_safe` 783, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 142, `hidden_symbols` 1,
doctests 89 merged and 387 standalone). Every llhttp test passes under ASan+UBSan, the
doctests included. Miri passes the 9 Rust-only tests (4 `unit_priv`, 5 `unit_pub`); each of
the 13 marked was run alone and stops at a foreign call, or, for `debug_trace`'s, at C's
`stderr` (`reads a C global`). TSan has no obligation: no `Send` or `Sync` claim and no thread;
nor has BSan, which nothing here is expected to trigger. The raw bindings changed, so the
crate was packaged (`--no-verify --exclude-lockfile`, 697 files) and built alone in bundled
mode with no variant, `glibc-bindings` and `ffibox` patched to their local sources and the
side campaigns' `plain` installs on `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR`, `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and
`PKG_CONFIG_PATH`. Usage cells are the assistant's.

I've landed the batch as `2a51ccb3f` on `crustify/waves/wave-194`, a fast-forward from `300c14dfc`. All 28 items are ported and the gates pass. Nothing is blocked.

**How the 28 items were ported**
- **13 items reuse what `llhttp.rs` already has.** These are the nine getters, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the three `HTTP_*_GEN` macros. Each is already an accessor or map method there (`parser_type`, `method`, `error`, `http_major`, `http_minor`, `status_code`, `upgrade`, `reason`, `error_offset`, `set_reason`, `Errno::constant_name`, `Method::map_string`, `Status::map_string`). Those methods now carry the item's `Replaces` anchor next to their own, so there is no duplicate API. The catch is that these 13 anchors live in `llhttp.rs`, not in their home `api.rs`.
- **The rest is new code in `api.rs`:**
  - `ParserMut::execute` (calls `parse`).
  - `pause`, `resume` and `resume_after_upgrade`, each acting only from the state C expects.
  - The ten `set_lenient_*(bool)` setters.
  - `ParserRef::debug_trace`, for `llhttp__debug`.
- **Exports:** C outside api.c calls six of these functions, so they have gateways under a new feature, `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, which is off. They are `llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_get_error_pos`, `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade` (from `httpparser.c`) and `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume`, `llhttp_get_error_reason` (from `httpparser.h`'s macros). Each is checked at compile time against its raw binding. I couldn't link-test them in place of `api.c.o`: that object still defines `llhttp_init` and the 23 dispatchers that batch 4 ports.

**`llhttp__debug`** is compiled into `api.c.o` on this build, but nothing calls it. The parser code in `llhttp.c` was generated without its debug mode, wavefront finds no callers, and no header declares it. So I ported it natively and did not export it. One C behaviour isn't copied: C prints a byte of 0x80 or more as `ffffff80` (a signed `char` through `%02x`, which C doesn't define). The Rust prints two digits; this is documented and covered by a unit test.

**Dependency routes, for their `confirmation`:**
- **`fprintf` and `stderr`:** `crustify-campaign` is confirmed. The trace has to go through C's own locked `stderr` stream so it stays in order with what the remaining C writes there; `std::io::stderr` writes the file descriptor directly and wouldn't keep that order. Nothing in the build's C reassigns, closes or unlocks `stderr`.
- **`abort` and `memset`:** `std` is confirmed. None of my items uses them; in api.c they belong to the name functions, `llhttp_finish` and `llhttp_settings_init`, which are batch 4's.

**Tests and gates**
- New tests: 4 `unit_priv`, 13 `unit_pub`, 2 `ub_safe`, 4 `equiv` and 3 doctests.
- clippy with warnings denied passes with the export feature off and on.
- Nightly fmt: my files are clean; `build.rs` already had a diff at the base.
- The whole workspace passes on `plain`.
- All llhttp tests pass under ASan+UBSan.
- Miri passes the 10 Rust-only tests; I ran each of the 13 tests marked to skip under Miri alone and confirmed it stops at C.
- The package builds on its own in bundled mode.
- `api.rs` is fully covered. `api.c` goes from 184 to 264 of its 283 lines; `llhttp__debug` is the one function no test reaches, since nothing calls it and it has no raw binding.
- I didn't run BSan or TSan; nothing in this batch calls for either.
- I also added 25 pointer findings to the ownership store; the change only adds records.

**Rerun after landing:** the wave tip had not moved, so there was no rebase. The tree I pushed is the one the gates ran on. Under the lock I reran only the llhttp tests, on `plain` and ASan+UBSan, because `debug_line` was rewritten after the first full runs (to avoid `format_args!`). The rest couldn't have changed: that rewrite touches only that one function, and the other change since then was the Miri skip reason on one test.

**Proposals filed** (both open, no spec change made):
- `crustify/evolution/port-onto-an-existing-accessor`, on `porting-symbols`: the rule I followed for the 13 reused items.
- `crustify/evolution/std-macro-expansions-outside-regions`, on the conventions and ffimap: std's `format_args!` and `thread_local!` count as unsafe code outside the regions. That has now forced a rewrite in three llhttp batches, including this one.

**Dashboard:** I filled the Symbols rows and Σ rows, Coverage stats, the Overview LoC and a Notes entry. Usage cells are left for you. I also set `ported symbols` to 60 at 6.13 %; the recorded 2.66 % didn't match its count of 32.

Scratch builds are deleted; `crustify/tmp` is down to 395 KB.
